title: Muhammad Ali Jinnah's birth chart
metaDescription: Muhammad Ali Jinnah's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 3.9° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.4° separates the Sun and Saturn from an exact sextile; at that range identity and structure read as one mechanism. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 3.9° Capricorn, inside the first decan (0°–10°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Saturn. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 15.7° Capricorn, Venus at 1.9° Sagittarius, Mars at 16.7° Scorpio. Mercury in an earth sign reads as thought with its feet on the ground; Venus in a fire sign reads as attraction declared rather than implied; Mars in a water sign reads as effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins the Sun and Saturn — a sextile holding at 0.4°. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Saturn sextile Neptune at 0.9°, and Mercury sextile Mars at 1.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags two placements in this chart. Mars in Scorpio at 16.7° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 17.5° is in domicile. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 earth, 4 fire, 2 water; by modality, 4 fixed, 3 cardinal, 3 mutable. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aries for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.0° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 19.5°.
